description: Search the jobs that match the user's résumé and filters, best match first, a page at a time. Leaves out jobs already applied to unless include_applied is true, and postings open only to nationals unless the profile lists a nationality or nationals_only says otherwise. Reads only.

city.description: City the posting is in, e.g. "Dubai" or "London".

country.description: Country name or ISO code, e.g. "US", "United Kingdom", "AE".

include_applied.description: Include jobs already applied to; they are left out otherwise.

min_salary.description: Only jobs stating pay of at least this; a job with no stated salary is left out.

min_score.description: Only jobs the résumé matches at least this well; leave it out for no floor.

nationals_only.description: Whether postings open only to a country's nationals are left out, included, or the only ones kept; leaving it out excludes them unless the profile lists a nationality.

offset.description: Rows to skip for the next page: the previous page's coverage names the offset to pass.

posted_since.description: ISO date; only jobs posted on or after it. Jobs with no known posting date are left out.

query.description: Words in the title, employer or description.

salary_currency.description: ISO code of the currency the stated pay must be in: with min_salary the floor is read in that currency, on its own it keeps the jobs that state pay in it.

seniority.description: Seniority as postings state it, e.g. "senior", "junior", "lead".

sort.description: Order of the page: best match first, or newest posting first.

workplace.description: Where the work is done; leave it out for any.

name: search_jobs

coverage.description: What this page covers, so the assistant can say honestly what it read.

complete.description: True when this page holds every matching row and no earlier page was skipped.

empty_reason.description: Why nothing came back, when the page is empty; null when it holds rows.

gaps.description: What this result does not hold, one entry per gap.

items.description: One kind of row this result does not hold.

kind.description: Why the row is missing: "page" for later rows, "earlier_pages" for rows before this page, "filtered" for rows a filter left out.

what.description: The gap in words: the offset to ask for next, or what was filtered out.

line.description: One sentence saying what this page holds, what was left out and what was not read; show it to the user as it is.

total.description: How many rows the filters match in all, when that is known.

jobs.description: The page of matching jobs, best match first or newest first as asked.

items.description: One job row: its facts, its match assessment and the start of its text.

apply_supported.description: Whether ApplySent can fill and submit this posting's form by itself.

apply_url.description: The employer's posting URL, where the application is filled.

country.description: Country the posting is in, as the catalogue recorded it.

excerpt.description: The start of the posting's text, plain, for a list row.

id.description: The job id the other job tools take.

match.description: The assessment of this job against the user's résumé, targets and eligibility.

additionalProperties.description: Points this factor added to the score.

breakdown.description: Points each match factor added; a full job read carries them, a list row does not.

eligible.description: Whether the user may take this job: work authorization, language and the posting's stated requirements all pass.

missing.description: What the assessment could not establish about the user for this posting; a full job read carries it, a list row does not.

items.description: One fact the assessment could not establish about the user.

notes.description: Notes the assessment kept beside the score; a full job read carries them, a list row does not.

items.description: One note the assessment kept beside the score.

reasons.description: Why the job scores what it does, in words.

items.description: One reason the job scored as it did.

score.description: Match score from 0 to 100 against the user's résumé and targets; higher is better.

posted_at.description: When the posting went up, ISO 8601 in UTC, when the catalogue knows it.

provider.description: The employer's hiring system the posting came from, e.g. workday, greenhouse or ashby.

salary.description: The pay the posting states, or null when it states none.

currency.description: ISO code of the stated pay.

max.description: Highest amount the posting states, in the currency's units.

min.description: Lowest amount the posting states, in the currency's units.

period.description: What the amounts are for (year, month, week, day or hour) when the posting states a period ApplySent recognizes.

saved.description: Whether the user saved this job.

title.description: The posting's title as the employer states it.

more.description: True when later pages hold more jobs.

offset.description: The offset this page starts at.

total.description: How many jobs the filters match in all.

title: Search matching jobs
